title: The Supreme Court Tests Its Own Limits on Guns

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重新审视者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶时代夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上，你都要带上 300 件你最珍爱的藏品去上班，你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满活力的、由美丽的 50 年前老物件组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新审视者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》的我是萨布丽娜·塔维内西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A critical gun case was argued before the Supreme Court this week, one of the few in modern history.
sentences.zh: 本周，最高法院审理了一起至关重要的枪支案件，这也是现代历史上为数不多的此类案件之一。

sentences.en: But instead of opening further freedoms for gun owners, the court, with its conservative supermajority, seemed ready to set a limit.
sentences.zh: 但拥有保守派绝对多数的法院，似乎并没有为枪支所有者开辟更多的自由，而是准备设定限制。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Adam Liptak explains.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事亚当·利普塔克将为我们做详细解读。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, November 9th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 11 月 9 日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, Adam, we've just had oral arguments in a very important gun case.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，我们刚刚结束了一个非常重要的枪支案件的口头辩论。

sentences.en: And you previewed it for us in October, and it was going to be one of those tests of just how far to the right this court was going to go.
sentences.zh: 你在 10 月份曾为我们做过前瞻报道，这将是对这座法院究竟会向右倾斜到何种程度的一次考验。

sentences.en: So, I've been watching your reporting, saw the case come up, and I wanted to give listeners a real sense of what the answer to that question might be.
sentences.zh: 因此，我一直在关注你的报道，看到这个案子开庭了，我想让听众真正了解这个问题的答案可能是什么。

sentences.en: So, let's dig into it.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: Remind us why this case is so important.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下，为什么这个案子如此重要。

sentences.en: So, this case is important on two levels.
sentences.zh: 这个案子在两个层面都很重要。

sentences.en: First level, very important.
sentences.zh: 第一层，非常重要。

sentences.en: Second level, even more important.
sentences.zh: 第二层，更加重要。

sentences.en: The very important question the court is looking at is,
sentences.zh: 法院正在审视的这个非常重要的问题是：

sentences.en: can the government make it a crime for someone to have a gun if they're the subject of a domestic violence restraining order?
sentences.zh: 如果一个人是家庭暴力限制令的对象，政府能否将其拥有枪支定为犯罪？

sentences.en: The presence of firearms combined with domestic strife is a recipe for lethal violence.
sentences.zh: 枪支的存在加上家庭纠纷，是导致致命暴力的温床。

sentences.en: So, the answer to that question, very important.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个问题的答案非常重要。

sentences.en: Even more important, though, is the way the court is going to approach that question.
sentences.zh: 不过，更重要的是法院将如何对待这个问题。

sentences.en: Because not long ago, in 2022, it announced a new Second Amendment standard by which to judge all kinds of gun control measures, one that is rooted in history.
sentences.zh: 因为不久前的 2022 年，它宣布了一个新的宪法第二修正案标准，用来衡量各种枪支管制措施，这个标准根植于历史。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, the Bruin decision, which we've talked about a bunch on the show.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是我们在节目中讨论过多次的“布鲁恩案”判决。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: this kind of revolutionary decision that really threw all of the cards up in the air because this historical requirement seemed to make it much harder to put new limits on guns.
sentences.zh: 这种革命性的判决把所有的牌都打乱了，因为这种历史要求似乎让对枪支施加新的限制变得更加困难。

sentences.en: So, it was really a big win, potentially, for gun rights advocates.
sentences.zh: 因此，对枪支权利倡导者来说，这绝对是一个潜在的巨大胜利。

sentences.en: It sure looked that way.
sentences.zh: 看起来确实如此。

sentences.en: What the court told us last year is that in judging whether a gun control measure is constitutional or not,
sentences.zh: 法院去年告诉我们的是，在判断一项枪支管制措施是否符合宪法时，

sentences.en: courts are supposed to look at the founding era and see if there were analogous restrictions back then.
sentences.zh: 法院应该审视建国时期，看看当时是否有类似的限制。

sentences.en: Whether in the 1700s there were regulations that addressed, say, domestic violence or whatever.
sentences.zh: 看看 1700 年代是否有针对家庭暴力或其他类似问题的法规。

sentences.en: However, and the court said, it doesn't have to be a perfect match, but it has to be analogous.
sentences.zh: 然而，法院表示，它不必是完全匹配的，但必须是类似的。

sentences.en: And that, even as I say it, it's hard to put your finger on exactly what that means.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使我说出这话时，也很难确切指出这到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: So, using that historical test has caused both confusion and a mountain of work for lower court judges who are not historians.
sentences.zh: 因此，使用这种历史测试给并非历史学家的下级法院法官带来了困惑和成山的工作。

sentences.en: You know, who are meant now to, you know, find parchment documents written in quill pen that may or may not match up with some contemporary law.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们现在必须去寻找用羽毛笔书写的羊皮纸文献，这些文献可能与现行法律相符，也可能不符。

sentences.en: It's what one judge called a game of historical where's Waldo of trying to find restrictions that more or less match up to contemporary restrictions.
sentences.zh: 正如一位法官所说，这就像是一场历史版的“威利在哪里”游戏，试图找到或多或少与当代限制相匹配的限制。

sentences.en: And just in the year after Bruin, courts have more than two dozen times struck down gun control laws because they couldn't find historical analogies.
sentences.zh: 就在“布鲁恩案”之后的短短一年里，由于找不到历史类似案例，法院已经有二十多次推翻了枪支管制法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, that's the landscape that the courts have been navigating for the past year, a big effect with this new standard, which brings us to the case argued this week.
sentences.zh: 这就是过去一年来法院一直在驾驭的格局，这一新标准产生了巨大影响，这就引出了本周开庭审理的案件。

sentences.en: I remember when we last talked about it, the guy at the center of the case was pretty unsympathetic.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们上次讨论时，案子核心的那个人实在是不怎么招人喜欢。

sentences.en: Remind us of the details.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们一下细节。

sentences.en: So, the case is called United States v.
sentences.zh: 这个案子被称为“美国诉

sentences.en: Rahimi.
sentences.zh: 拉希米案”。

sentences.en: It concerns a young man named Zaki Rahimi, who a few years ago physically assaulted his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 它涉及一名叫扎基·拉希米的年轻男子，几年前他曾对女友实施身体暴力。

sentences.en: She seeks a restraining order.
sentences.zh: 她寻求限制令。

sentences.en: A judge grants the restraining order, saying that Rahimi is likely to commit violence again.
sentences.zh: 法官批准了限制令，称拉希米很可能会再次实施暴力。

sentences.en: And that restraining order also tells him that he can't have guns.
sentences.zh: 而且该限制令还告诉他，他不能拥有枪支。

sentences.en: And if he is found possessing a gun, that would be a federal crime.
sentences.zh: 如果发现他拥有枪支，那将构成联邦重罪。

sentences.en: But that doesn't stop Rahimi from committing a string of gun crimes.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止拉希米进行一连串的涉枪犯罪。

sentences.en: In one case, he takes a shot at a fellow driver in a road rage incident.
sentences.zh: 在其中一起事件中，他在路怒事件中向另一名司机开枪。

sentences.en: In another, after someone is talking trash about him in social media, as he put it, he shoots a gun into that person's house.
sentences.zh: 在另一起事件中，正如他所说，有人在社交媒体上说他的坏话后，他向那个人的房子开枪。

sentences.en: After a friend's credit card was declined at a Whataburger fast food restaurant, he takes out a gun and fires several shots into the air.
sentences.zh: 在一家德克萨斯汉堡快餐店，朋友的信用卡被拒付后，他掏出一枪向空中开了几枪。

sentences.en: Luckily, nobody was killed during these incidents.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，在这些事件中没有人丧生。

sentences.en: But Zaki Rahimi was a one-man crime spree.
sentences.zh: 但扎基·拉希米简直是一个人的犯罪狂欢。

sentences.en: And so, these incidents draw the attention of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些事件引起了执法部门的注意。

sentences.en: The authorities search his home.
sentences.zh: 当局搜查了他的家。

sentences.en: They find guns.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了枪支。

sentences.en: They find a copy of the restraining order that says he can't have guns.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了一份限制令的复印件，上面写着他不能拥有枪支。

sentences.en: And he's charged with the federal crime of possessing guns while being subject to a domestic violence restraining order.
sentences.zh: 他被指控犯有在受到家庭暴力限制令约束的同时拥有枪支的联邦罪行。

sentences.en: And he's convicted.
sentences.zh: 并且他被定罪了。

sentences.en: And he gets a pretty stiff prison sentence.
sentences.zh: 他被判处了相当严厉的监禁刑期。

sentences.en: So, he challenges that ruling in federal court.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在联邦法院对该裁决提出了挑战。

sentences.en: And, you know, gun rights groups do not love this because he's the least sympathetic possible protagonist in a Second Amendment case.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，枪支权利组织并不喜欢这样，因为他是第二修正案案件中最不讨人喜欢的原告。

sentences.en: And the lower courts initially ruled against Rahimi, said he could be prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 下级法院最初对拉希米做出不利裁决，称他可以被起诉。

sentences.en: So, he loses in a district court.
sentences.zh: 所以，他在地区法院败诉了。

sentences.en: He loses in an appeals court.
sentences.zh: 他在上诉法院败诉了。

sentences.en: But then Bruin happens, Rahimi goes back to the appeals court, and the appeals court under Bruin takes a fresh look at this question and concludes, wait a second,
sentences.zh: 但随后“布鲁恩案”发生了，拉希米回到了上诉法院，上诉法院在“布鲁恩案”的框架下重新审视了这个问题，并得出结论：等一下，

sentences.en: we can't find a historical analog that closely matches up to domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 我们找不到与家庭暴力紧密匹配的历史类似案例。

sentences.en: And, therefore, they rule for Rahimi, and they strike down the law as unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们裁决拉希米胜诉，并以违宪为由推翻了该法律。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is a clear example of the legal earthquake we were talking about, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这显然是我们之前讨论过的法律大地震的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, the historical standard was actually used to overturn the law that Rahimi had been jailed under.
sentences.zh: 比如，历史标准实际上被用来推翻拉希米被关入监狱时所依据的法律。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, the Biden administration takes the case to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以，拜登政府将此案闹到了最高法院。

sentences.en: They're probably delighted in one sense that they have such a sympathetic case to take to the court.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们可能很高兴能把这样一个深得民心的案件带到最高法院。

sentences.en: And the justices accept the case, as they almost always do, when a lower court has struck down a federal law.
sentences.zh: 大法官们受理了这个案子，就像下级法院推翻联邦法律时他们几乎总是做的那样。

sentences.en: I think the justices think that if anyone's going to be striking down federal laws as unconstitutional, it ought to be the Supreme Court and not lower courts.
sentences.zh: 我认为大法官们认为，如果要由谁来以违宪为由推翻联邦法律，那也应该由最高法院来做，而不是下级法院。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's how the case shot up to the Supreme Court, and that brings us to the oral arguments that you heard this week.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是案件是如何一路冲到最高法院的，这也把我们带到了你本周听到的口头辩论。

sentences.en: So, you were there, Adam.
sentences.zh: 亚当，你当时也在场。

sentences.en: Tell me how they began.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他们是如何开始的。

sentences.en: So, the Biden administration took the case to the court, and they get to go firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，拜登政府把这个案子带到了法院，他们可以先发言。

sentences.en: General Proliger?
sentences.zh: 普雷洛格总检察长？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court, guns and domestic abuse are a deadly combination.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法官大人，枪支和家庭虐待是致命的组合。

sentences.en: They're represented by Elizabeth Proliger, the Solicitor General of the United States, the Justice Department official, whose job it is to argue cases before the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他们由美国副总检察长、司法部官员伊丽莎白·普雷洛格代表，她的职责是在最高法院出庭辩论案件。

sentences.en: And she talks to the justices very much in the language of Bruin, in the language of history.
sentences.zh: 她与大法官们的对话大量使用了“布鲁恩案”的语言，使用了历史的语言。

sentences.en: Like Heller and McDonald, Bruin recognized that Congress may disarm those who are not law-abiding, responsible citizens.
sentences.zh: 就像海勒案和麦克唐纳案一样，“布鲁恩案”承认国会可以解除那些并非守法、负责任的公民的武装。

sentences.en: That principle is firmly grounded in the Second Amendment's history and tradition throughout our nation's history.
sentences.zh: 这一原则在我们国家历史上的第二修正案历史和传统中有着坚实的基础。

sentences.en: She draws on earlier Supreme Court decisions,
sentences.zh: 她借鉴了最高法院先前的判决，

sentences.en: which have used a phrase that says the Second Amendment protects law-abiding and responsible citizens and gives them a right to keep and bear arMs.
sentences.zh: 这些判决曾使用过这样一句话：第二修正案保护守法和负责任的公民，并赋予他们拥有和携带武器的权利。

sentences.en: And she bears down on that phrase.
sentences.zh: 她紧紧围绕着这句话展开。

sentences.en: This case focuses on the not-responsible citizens principle.
sentences.zh: 本案关注的是“不负责任的公民”原则。

sentences.en: She says she's not focused in this case on law-abiding, but she is focused on responsible.
sentences.zh: 她说，她在这个案子中关注的不是守法，而是负责任。

sentences.en: And initially, there's some resistance to that, particularly from the chief justice.
sentences.zh: 最初，对此有一些阻力，尤其是来自首席大法官。

sentences.en: Responsibility is a very broad concept.
sentences.zh: 责任是一个非常广泛的概念。

sentences.en: I mean, not taking your recycling to the curb on Thursdays.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，周四没有把回收物品拿到路边去。

sentences.en: He thinks that responsible is too vague a phrase.
sentences.zh: 他认为“负责任”这个词太模糊了。

sentences.en: He says, well, what if I don't take out the recycling?
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，如果我不拿回收物出去呢？

sentences.en: I suppose I'm not responsible.
sentences.zh: 我想我就是不负责任。

sentences.en: What if I get in a fight at a ballgame?
sentences.zh: 如果我在球赛里打架呢？

sentences.en: I suppose I'm not responsible.
sentences.zh: 我想我就是不负责任。

sentences.en: What seems irresponsible to some people might seem like, well, that's not a big deal to others.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说不负责任的事，在其他人看来可能觉得没什么大不了。

sentences.en: So what is the model?
sentences.zh: 那么标准是什么？

sentences.en: And she says...
sentences.zh: 她说……

sentences.en: So I want to be really clear that we're not using the term not responsible to describe, colloquially,
sentences.zh: 所以我想要非常明确地指出，我们使用“不负责任”这个词，在日常口语中并不是指

sentences.en: anyone who you might describe as demonstrating irresponsibility in many of those contexts that you just described in your hypotheticals.
sentences.zh: 任何你可能在刚才你所假设的那些情境中表现出不负责任的人。

sentences.en: It's actually kind of a term of art.
sentences.zh: 这其实算是一个专业术语。

sentences.en: ...intrinsically tied to the danger you would present if you have access to firearMs.
sentences.zh: ...与你如果拥有枪支就会带来的危险密不可分。

sentences.en: And I would draw...
sentences.zh: 我会得出……

sentences.en: It's actually a way of talking about whether people are dangerous or not.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是讨论人们是否危险的一种方式。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Responsible people are not dangerous people.
sentences.zh: 负责任的人不是危险的人。

sentences.en: And if you can show that someone is dangerous, there are general laws from the founding era that allow the government to disarm people who are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 如果你能证明某人是危险的，建国时期就有一般性法律允许政府解除危险人物的武装。

sentences.en: And that seems to get a lot of traction.
sentences.zh: 这似乎引起了很大的共鸣。

sentences.en: How do you know?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道？

sentences.en: I mean, I think there would be a little dispute that someone who was guilty, say, or even had a restraining order, that domestic violence is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为对于有罪的人，或者甚至有限制令在身的人，家庭暴力是危险的，这一点几乎没有什么争议。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So someone who poses a risk of domestic violence is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 因此，构成家庭暴力风险的人是危险的。

sentences.en: So in other words, to bring this back to the historical standards set by Bruin,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，为了回到“布鲁恩案”设定的历史标准，

sentences.en: rather than finding some exact one-to-one law in the books about domestic violence from way back when,
sentences.zh: 普雷洛格并没有去寻找过去关于家庭暴力的确切一一对应的法律，

sentences.en: Prelugger is basically saying it was clear that there were laws stating the general principle that dangerous people should not have guns.
sentences.zh: 而是基本上在说，很明显当时存在阐明一般原则的法律，即危险分子不应拥有枪支。

sentences.en: And we can apply that principle to domestic violence cases in the present day.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将这一原则应用到当今的家庭暴力案件中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To rely on founding era laws, but at a high level of generality.
sentences.zh: 依靠建国时期的法律，但在高度概括的层面上。

sentences.en: So they're not talking about domestic violence as such, but they're talking about you can disarm dangerous individuals.
sentences.zh: 所以他们谈论的不是狭义上的家庭暴力，而是你可以解除危险个人的武装。

sentences.en: And that mode of argument by Prelugger seemed to really work with most of the conservative justices.
sentences.zh: 普雷洛格的这种辩论方式似乎确实对大多数保守派大法官起到了作用。

sentences.en: Do you think the level of generality, I take your point, you've got surety laws, you've got afraid laws, you've got a lot of historical evidence.
sentences.zh: 你认为概括的程度——我理解你的观点，你有担保法，你有恐惧法，你有很多历史证据。

sentences.en: Because they could rule in favor of the law and against Rahimi without doing damage to their general project of making the Second Amendment be a subject of a history teSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们可以在不损害让第二修正案成为历史测试主题的总体规划的情况下，做出有利于法律并反对拉希明的裁决。

sentences.en: Okay, so interestingly, some of the conservative justices are coming around on the case, but what about Clarence Thomas, who's, of course,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，一些保守派大法官在这个案子上开始转变态度，但克拉伦斯·托马斯呢，当然，

sentences.en: the most conservative justice and actually wrote the majority opinion on Bruin?
sentences.zh: 他是最保守的大法官，实际上还撰写了“布鲁恩案”的多数意见书？

sentences.en: So, Sabrina, Clarence Thomas and, to a large extent, the other most conservative justice, Samuel Alito, seemed not to really like where this was going.
sentences.zh: 所以，萨布丽娜，克拉伦斯·托马斯，以及很大程度上另一位最保守的大法官塞缪尔·阿利托，似乎真的不喜欢事情朝这个方向发展。

sentences.en: What if someone, this is a civil action, I think we could agree on the, if these were criminal proceedings.
sentences.zh: 如果有人——这是一起民事诉讼，我想我们可以在这一点上达成一致，如果这是刑事诉讼的话。

sentences.en: They're not convinced that there's enough due process in abbreviated civil domestic violence hearings.
sentences.zh: 他们不确信在简短的民事家庭暴力听证会中有足够的正当程序。

sentences.en: If this were a criminal proceeding, then you would have a determination of what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一起刑事诉讼，那么你就会对你所谈论的事情做出裁决。

sentences.en: Someone would be convicted of a crime, a felony, assault or something.
sentences.zh: 某人会被判犯有罪行、重罪、攻击罪或诸如此类。

sentences.en: But here you have something that's anticipatory or predictive, where a court, a civil court, is making the determination.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，你有一些具有前瞻性或预测性的东西，法院、民事法院正在做出裁决。

sentences.en: And I think they were nervous that this great project of Bruin might be undermined by the eventual decision in the Rahimi case.
sentences.zh: 我想他们很紧张，“布鲁恩案”的宏伟蓝图可能会被拉希米案的最终裁决所破坏。

sentences.en: And what about the liberal justices?
sentences.zh: 那自由派大法官呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm assuming that they were pretty happy to have the center of the court agreeing with the Biden administration on the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜他们会很高兴看到法院核心层在这个案子上同意拜登政府的意见。

sentences.en: Well, the liberal justices, of course, are happy to sustain most gun control laws and they will vote for the government and against Rahimi.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自由派大法官当然很高兴维持大多数枪支管制法，他们会投票支持政府并反对拉希米。

sentences.en: But they also use the argument and might like to use the case to make a broader point.
sentences.zh: 但他们也使用了这一论点，并可能希望利用这个案子来表达更广泛的观点。

sentences.en: Can I ask you a question about that, though?
sentences.zh: 不过我能就此问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: I guess I'm trying to understand whether we can really be analyzing this consistent with the Bruin teSt.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在试图理解我们是否真的能以与“布鲁恩测试”一致的方式来分析这一点。

sentences.en: To question whether this history-based standard makes any sense.
sentences.zh: 去质疑这种基于历史的标准是否有任何意义。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to understand how the Bruin test works in a situation in which there is at least some evidence that domestic violence was not considered to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 我只是想了解在以下情况下“布鲁恩测试”是如何运作的：至少有一些证据表明，家庭暴力在当时并没有被认为，你知道的，

sentences.en: subject to the kinds of regulation that it is today.
sentences.zh: 受到今天那样的监管。

sentences.en: So Justice Ketanji Brown-Jackson, for instance, was asking a series of questions about why are we looking at the founding era to begin with?
sentences.zh: 因此，比如大法官克坦吉·布朗·杰克逊提出了一系列问题：我们最初为什么要看建国时期？

sentences.en: What's the point of going to the founding era?
sentences.zh: 去建国时期的意义何在？

sentences.en: I mean, I thought it was doing some work, but if we're still applying modern sensibilities, I don't really understand the historical framing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我以为它在起作用，但如果我们仍然在应用现代的情感，我真的不理解这种历史框架。

sentences.en: So liberal justices are saying, hey, conservatives, we agree this law should stand, but we disagree that it's a narrow case.
sentences.zh: 所以自由派大法官在说，嘿，保守派们，我们同意这项法律应该保留，但我们不同意这是一个狭隘的案子。

sentences.en: Like we feel this leads to a broader question, which is the whole historical standard is kind of wrong.
sentences.zh: 就像我们觉得这引出了一个更广泛的问题，也就是整个历史标准在某种程度上是错误的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there's disagreement about how you get there, what rationale you use to uphold this law on domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于如何得出结论，以及用什么法理依据来维持这项关于家庭暴力的法律，大家的意见并不一致。

sentences.en: But there's seeming consensus that the answer has to be that the law is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 但似乎有一个共识，那就是答案必须是这项法律符合宪法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So it sounds like pretty much all of the justices, perhaps with the exception of Alito and Thomas, seem persuaded by pre-logger.
sentences.zh: 听起来几乎所有的法官，也许除了阿利托和托马斯之外，似乎都被普雷洛格说服了。

sentences.en: So what is the lawyer representing Rahimi and the gun rights side of the case argue?
sentences.zh: 那么，代表拉希米和本案中持枪权一方的律师是怎么辩论的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like he's going to have a pretty uphill battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来他将面临一场相当艰难的硬仗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Mr. Wright?
sentences.zh: 莱特先生？

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，首席大法官阁下，法官大人。

sentences.en: Rahimi's represented by a federal public defender named Matthew Wright.
sentences.zh: 拉希米的辩护律师是一位名叫马修·莱特的联邦公设辩护人。

sentences.en: He argues second.
sentences.zh: 他是第二个进行辩论的。

sentences.en: And by the time he gets up, his central argument has been cut out from under him.
sentences.zh: 当他站起来发言时，他的核心论点已经被釜底抽薪了。

sentences.en: It feels like what the government is doing is looking down the dark well of American history and seeing only a reflection of itself in the 20th and 21st century and saying that's what history shows.
sentences.zh: 感觉政府的做法就像是看着美国历史那口幽暗的水井，却只在20和21世纪看到了自己的倒影，然后说这就是历史展现的面貌。

sentences.en: I think he was prepared to argue that there's no analogous ban from the founding era and therefore he wins.
sentences.zh: 我想他原本准备辩称，建国时期没有类似的禁令，因此他会赢。

sentences.en: That argument undermines so much in the first half of the argument,
sentences.zh: 这个论点破坏了前半部分辩论中的许多内容，

sentences.en: left him a little unfocused and a little unsure about how to answer a series of questions from the justices about the implications of his position in other settings.
sentences.zh: 这让他显得有点不在状态，对于法官们关于他的立场在其他场景下会有什么影响的一系列提问，也有些不知如何回答。

sentences.en: Do you think that the Congress can disarm people who are mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 你认为国会可以解除精神病患者的武装吗？

sentences.en: Setting aside an enumerated powers problem, so they're in the District of Columbia or something like that.
sentences.zh: 抛开列举权力的问题不谈，假设他们在华盛顿特区或类似的地方。

sentences.en: And his answers...
sentences.zh: 而他的回答……

sentences.en: Let me be honest truth, Mr. Wright.
sentences.zh: 说句实话，莱特先生。

sentences.en: I feel like you're running away from your argument.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在回避自己的论点。

sentences.en: ...did not satisfy many of the justices.
sentences.zh: ……并没有让许多法官满意。

sentences.en: I mean, is that the position you really want to take?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是你想持有的立场吗？

sentences.en: So it was a different tone in the second half of the argument.
sentences.zh: 所以辩论的后半段基调变了。

sentences.en: I'm so confused because I thought your argument...
sentences.zh: 我很困惑，因为我以为你的论点……

sentences.en: ...where you had a less assured performance by someone who does not appear to be an appellate specialiSt.
sentences.zh: ……一个看起来并非上诉专家的表现不太自信的人。

sentences.en: And there was a very telling exchange...
sentences.zh: 当时有一段非常说明问题的对话……

sentences.en: Well, to the extent that's pertinent, you don't have any doubt that your client's a dangerous person, do you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，就相关性而言，你对你的当事人是个危险人物这一点毫无疑问，对吧？

sentences.en: The Chief Justice said, well, you agree that your client is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官说，嗯，你承认你的当事人是危险的。

sentences.en: Your Honor, I would want to know what dangerous person means.
sentences.zh: 法官阁下，我想知道“危险人物”是什么意思。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, someone who's shooting, you know, at people, that's a good start.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，朝别人开枪的人，这算是个很好的开始。

sentences.en: So, that's fair.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很公平。

sentences.en: I'll say this.
sentences.zh: 我这么说吧。

sentences.en: You know, at that point where the Chief Justice of the United States is saying your client is dangerous because he goes around shooting at people,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当美国首席大法官指出你的当事人因为到处朝人开枪而具有危险性时，

sentences.en: you have an uphill fight ahead of you.
sentences.zh: 你面前将是一场苦战。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So, by the end of the argument, you had one very assured performance, one that was the opposite of that performance,
sentences.zh: 所以，到辩论结束时，你们看到的是一种非常自信的表现，一种与那种表现截然相反的表现，

sentences.en: and a host of open questions about how they're going to rule in this particular case, and how that ruling will impact gun laws in countless other cases.
sentences.zh: 以及一堆悬而未决的问题：他们将如何在这个特定案件中做出裁决，以及这一裁决将如何影响无数其他案件中的枪支法律。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 探索太空七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next start.
sentences.zh: 我们想要看看下一个起点之外是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，陪伴您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: So, Adam, you've described a pretty lopsided day in court with the Solicitor General laying a framework that most of the justices agreed with.
sentences.zh: 亚当，那么你刚才描述了法庭上相当一边倒的一天，副总检察长奠定了大多数法官都赞同的框架。

sentences.en: What's your sense of how the court's going to rule?
sentences.zh: 你对法院会如何裁决有什么看法？

sentences.en: I separate the court into three blocks.
sentences.zh: 我把法院分为三个阵营。

sentences.en: There's the middle of the court.
sentences.zh: 中间派法官。

sentences.en: The three Trump justices, Gorsuch, Barrett, and Kavanaugh, and the chief justice, Republican appointees, but by the standards of this Supreme Court, relatively moderate.
sentences.zh: 三位特朗普任命的法官戈萨奇、巴雷特和卡瓦诺，以及首席大法官，他们是共和党任命的，但以最高法院的标准来看，相对温和。

sentences.en: And they will probably try to write a decision as narrow as they can, upholding this law and kicking every other question about it down the road.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会尽量写出一份范围窄得多的裁决，维持这项法律，并把关于它的所有其他问题都推迟以后再说。

sentences.en: The liberals, Kagan, Sotomayor, and Jackson, will agree that the law should be upheld, but they will almost certainly say, hey, it's time to rethink whether this new construct,
sentences.zh: 自由派法官卡根、索托马约尔和杰克逊将同意维持该法律，但他们几乎肯定会说，嘿，是时候重新思考这种新架构了，

sentences.en: this new test from Bruin, makes any sense at all.
sentences.zh: 也就是布鲁因案中的这个新测试，到底有没有任何意义。

sentences.en: And then on the far right side of the court,
sentences.zh: 然后在法院的最右翼，

sentences.en: Justices Thomas and Alito will either dissent or issue a grudging concurrence in which they will try to make the point that they meant what Justice Thomas said in Bruin,
sentences.zh: 托马斯和阿利托法官要么会发表异议，要么会发表一份勉强赞同的意见，在其中试图阐明他们的观点：他们是认真的，正如托马斯法官在布鲁因案中所说的那样，

sentences.en: that unlike other parts of the Bill of Rights, this is a part of the Bill of Rights that should be understood purely as a historical matter.
sentences.zh: 与《权利法案》的其他部分不同，这是《权利法案》中应该纯粹从历史角度来理解的一部分。

sentences.en: But Adam, if that's how the decision is written, is this actually that narrow of a ruling?
sentences.zh: 但是亚当，如果判决是这样写的，这真的算是一个很窄的裁决吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you'd mentioned that the middle of the road conservative justices were kind of agreeing to this principle idea that Priligar was suggesting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提到温和派保守派法官在某种程度上赞同普雷洛格提出的这一原则性观点。

sentences.en: So it seems like that could actually open the door for gun control groups to try to do all sorts of new stuff, like no need to find a historical twin anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来这实际上可能会为控枪组织打开大门，让他们尝试各种新花样，比如不再需要寻找历史上的孪生案例了。

sentences.en: It will depend a lot on how it's written.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于判决书的具体写法。

sentences.en: People will make use of it as best they can.
sentences.zh: 人们会尽其所能地利用它。

sentences.en: But you're right to say that to the extent you're going to be able to discern general principles, not dead ringers, not historical twins,
sentences.zh: 但你说得对，就你能辨别出一般原则（而不是绝对相似的案例、不是历史上的孪生案例）而言，

sentences.en: that moves it away from the conservative legal movement's way of thinking about the Constitution, which is an effort to unearth its original meaning.
sentences.zh: 这就偏离了保守派法律运动对宪法的思考方式，即发掘其原始含义的努力。

sentences.en: And more in the way liberals like to think about the Constitution as a living document that sets out general principles that succeeding generations can use to address contemporary probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而更偏向于自由派喜欢思考宪法的方式，即把它视为一本活的宪法文件，其中规定了一般原则，后代可以利用这些原则来解决当代问题。

sentences.en: It's almost as if Priligar has sort of moved the goal line on the standard, right?
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是普雷洛格在标准上移动了球门，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, in fairness to Justice Thomas, in his opinion in Bruin, he did say that there are two kinds of analogies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，公平地说，托马斯法官在布鲁因案的意见中确实说过有两种类比。

sentences.en: There's one that is a reasonable fit, and there's the other that, as he said, is a twin, a dead ringer.
sentences.zh: 一种是合理的契合，另一种正如他所说，是一个孪生案例、一个绝对相似的案例。

sentences.en: And he said you only need the reasonable fit.
sentences.zh: 他说你只需要合理的契合。

sentences.en: But what that reasonable fit is and how broad the principles you can draw on from history,
sentences.zh: 但什么是合理的契合，以及你可以从历史中汲取的原则有多广泛，

sentences.en: this will be a challenge for whoever writes the majority opinion, almost certainly a conservative, because they will both have to adopt parts of the Solicitor General's argument,
sentences.zh: 对于撰写多数意见书的人来说，这将是一个挑战，几乎可以肯定是一位保守派法官，因为他们既必须采纳副总检察长论点的部分内容，

sentences.en: but also not go too far in opening the door to all kinds of general principles that would sustain all kinds of gun laws.
sentences.zh: 又不能走得太远，以至于为各种能够支撑各类枪支法律的一般原则敞开大门。

sentences.en: So let's talk about what this case might mean for the future of gun laws in this country.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈这个案件对这个国家未来枪支法律可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: If the court rules in the way that you've indicated that it might, what does that mean for the future of Bruin and how the court considers gun regulation?
sentences.zh: 如果法院按照你所暗示的那样进行裁决，这对布鲁因案的未来以及法院如何审视枪支监管意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, Bruin's not going anywhere, Sabrina, and the history test is not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 嗯，布鲁因案不会消失，塞布丽娜，历史测试也不会消失。

sentences.en: And there's a ton of litigation.
sentences.zh: 而且有大量的诉讼。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of laws.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的法律。

sentences.en: Let me give you a couple of cases that are already at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 我给你举几个已经送到最高法院的案件。

sentences.en: Petitions seeking review have been filed in these cases, and they present, I think, harder questions than Rahimi does.
sentences.zh: 这些案件已经提交了调卷令申请，我认为它们比拉希米案提出了更难的问题。

sentences.en: One asks whether a federal law that disarms felons, people who have committed serious crimes, is constitutional in every application.
sentences.zh: 其中一个案件询问：一项解除重罪犯（犯下严重罪行的个人）武装的联邦法律，在所有应用中是否都符合宪法。

sentences.en: And the guy bringing the case says, I made a false statement to obtain food stamps 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而提起诉讼的那个人说，我30年前为了领食品券做过虚假陈述。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That shouldn't prohibit me from having a gun.
sentences.zh: 这不应该剥夺我拥有枪支的权利。

sentences.en: And, you know, you're probably going to search the historical records in vain to find people lying about food stamps in the founding era.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在历史记录里大概也找不到建国时期有人为领食品券而说谎的记载。

sentences.en: Similarly, there's a federal law that disarms people who use illegal drugs.
sentences.zh: 同样，有一项联邦法律规定解除非法吸毒人员的武装。

sentences.en: And someone who uses marijuana, fairly heavily, but maybe no different than a social drink or drinks, has brought a case to the Supreme Court, having one in the lower courts,
sentences.zh: 有一个吸食大麻相当严重的人（也许和社交饮酒没什么两样，或者经常喝酒），他已经在下级法院赢了官司，并把案件闹到了最高法院，

sentences.en: saying he should not be disarmed because he's got a pot habit.
sentences.zh: 声称他不应该因为有吸大麻的习惯而被解除武装。

sentences.en: So, on their face, they're much more sympathetic cases for the gun rights advocates.
sentences.zh: 所以，从表面上看，这些对持枪权倡导者来说是更容易引起同情的案件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The bottom line is, just because Rahimi loses, as he probably will, doesn't mean these other people will lose.
sentences.zh: 底线是，拉希米输了（他很可能会输），并不意味着这其他人也会输。

sentences.en: There are countless cases in the lower courts challenging all kinds of gun laws.
sentences.zh: 下级法院有无数挑战各种枪支法律的案件。

sentences.en: And not only who can have guns, but also you can ask questions about where can you bring your gun?
sentences.zh: 不仅是谁能拥有枪支，你还可以提出关于你能在哪里带枪的问题？

sentences.en: Can you bring it to a school?
sentences.zh: 你能把它带到学校吗？

sentences.en: Can you bring it to a courthouse?
sentences.zh: 你能把它带到法院吗？

sentences.en: Can you bring it to the post office?
sentences.zh: 你能把它带到邮局吗？

sentences.en: Can you bring it to Yankee Stadium?
sentences.zh: 你能把它带到洋基体育场吗？

sentences.en: And then a third category, what kinds of guns?
sentences.zh: 然后是第三类，什么类型的枪？

sentences.en: So-called assault weapons, open question.
sentences.zh: 所谓的突击武器，这是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: Machine guns, probably not.
sentences.zh: 机枪，大概不行。

sentences.en: Handguns, apparently yes.
sentences.zh: 手枪，显然可以。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a million questions here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有一百万个问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this Rahimi case may have actually been a bridge too far, but what you're saying is there are a lot of other cases out there and a lot of other legal questions to be answered
sentences.zh: 这个拉希米案实际上可能已经走得太远了，但你的意思是，还有很多其他的案件以及很多其他有待解答的法律问题，

sentences.en: that may not, in the minds of this 6-3 conservative court, be taking it too far.
sentences.zh: 在由6比3保守派主导的最高法院看来，这些可能并不算走得太远。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it'll be very interesting to read, probably not till June, how exactly they grapple with the history test in Rahimi in a way that rules against Rahimi,
sentences.zh: 这将非常有趣，大概要到6月份才能读到，看看他们将如何在拉希米案中如何处理历史测试，既做出对拉希米不利的裁决，

sentences.en: but tries not to do substantial damage to their larger project of looking to history to decide whether gun laws are constitutional or not.
sentences.zh: 又尽量不损害他们利用历史来决定枪支法律是否合宪这一宏大计划。

sentences.en: Adam, you know, it strikes me that this is all very new, right?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你知道，我觉得这一切都非常新颖，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, we're in this new era of Second Amendment interpretation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们正处于第二修正案解释的新时代。

sentences.en: The court is now going to hear all of these new cases that figure out the details of what the right to bear arms actually means in practice.
sentences.zh: 法院现在将审理所有这些新案件，以弄清持枪权在实践中到底意味着什么细节。

sentences.en: You're quite right, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，塞布丽娜。

sentences.en: Remember, it was only in 2008, for the first time in the history of the Republic, that the Supreme Court recognized an individual right to keep and bear arMs.
sentences.zh: 记住，直到2008年，最高法院才在共和国历史上首次承认了个人拥有和携带武器的权利。

sentences.en: It's a very new individual right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常崭新的个人权利。

sentences.en: Then the court basically went silent for more than a decade until 2022 in Bruin announcing this new teSt.
sentences.zh: 然后法院基本上沉默了十多年，直到2022年的布鲁因案才宣布了这个新测试。

sentences.en: Now we have the first application of the new teSt.
sentences.zh: 现在我们迎来了这个新测试的首次应用。

sentences.en: So that's kind of three major Second Amendment cases in the history of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 所以这可以说是共和国历史上关于第二修正案的三个重大案件。

sentences.en: By contrast, in this term alone, there are five or six significant First Amendment cases.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，仅在本届任期内，就有五到六起重大的第一修正案案件。

sentences.en: And that's characteristic.
sentences.zh: 这也是它的特点。

sentences.en: The court has been explaining and refining the First Amendment for many decades.
sentences.zh: 法院几十年来一直在解释和完善第一修正案。

sentences.en: We're just at the beginning of the road for the Supreme Court to start to tell us what exactly is meant by the rights conferred by the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 最高法院才刚刚开始告诉我们第二修正案赋予的权利到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: And this Rahimi case will be a big step in the direction of trying to grapple with and understand this constitutional right.
sentences.zh: 而这个拉希米案将是努力应对和理解这一宪法权利的重要一步。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you.
sentences.zh: 亚当，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，塞布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“归类”（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作“拼字蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母方框”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才你听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the union representing tens of thousands of actors reached a tentative deal with entertainment companies in Hollywood on a contract.
sentences.zh: 周三，代表数万名演员的工会与好莱坞娱乐公司就一份合同达成了一项初步协议。

sentences.en: The agreement includes pay increases, healthcare funding, and agreements on how AI will be used.
sentences.zh: 该协议包括加薪、医疗保健资金以及关于如何使用人工智能的协议。

sentences.en: It comes more than a month after the Writers Guild of America negotiated its own deal and clears the way for the $134 billion American movie and television business
sentences.zh: 在此之前的一个多月，美国编剧工会刚刚谈判达成了自己的协议，这为产值达1340亿美元的美国电影和电视产业

sentences.en: to swing back into motion.
sentences.zh: 重新焕发活力扫清了道路。

sentences.en: And Secretary of State Antony Blinken said Wednesday that the Gaza Strip should be unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian authority once the war ends.
sentences.zh: 美国国务卿安东尼·布林肯周三表示，加沙地带在战争结束后应在巴勒斯坦权力机构领导下与约旦河西岸统一。

sentences.en: The strongest signal yet from the Biden administration about what it would like to see at the end of Israel's fight against Hamas in the enclave.
sentences.zh: 这是拜登政府迄今为止发出的最强烈信号，表明其希望看到以色列在该飞地打击哈马斯的行动结束时出现怎样的局面。

sentences.en: Blinken offered no details about how such an arrangement might be implemented.
sentences.zh: 布林肯没有透露如何实施这种安排的具体细节。

sentences.en: But restoring the Palestinian authority, which administers parts of the West Bank, to power in Gaza would not be easy, even if Israel managed to end Hamas's rule.
sentences.zh: 但是，即便以色列能够终结哈马斯的统治，要将管理约旦河西岸部分地区的巴勒斯坦权力机构重新推上加沙的权力宝座也绝非易事。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Will Reed, and Muj Zaydi.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科、威尔·里德和穆杰·扎伊迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Patricia Willards.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和帕特里夏·威拉德斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marianne Lozano.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛扎诺的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由艾丽莎·莫克斯利工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日简报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。
